product.name: open-wa
product.oneLine: Run one command and your WhatsApp number becomes an API you can call from any language: send messages, media and stickers, take bookings, send codes and answer calls.
product.how: It runs WhatsApp Web in a browser it controls (Puppeteer, Playwright, or the experimental Lightpanda driver) and exposes the account's chats, messages and events to your code.
product.since: GitHub repository created August 2019; first npm release April 2020
product.unofficial: Unofficial. Not affiliated with, authorised, maintained, sponsored or endorsed by WhatsApp, Meta or their affiliates.
product.risk: Automation tools can cause a WhatsApp account to be restricted or banned. You accept that risk when you use it.
product.terms: Using the project means you agree to the Terms of Service.

stats.note: Quote these with the date and source. Round down if you round (3.6k stars, 105k downloads a year). Never present them as users or customers.

firstRun: Run the command. It starts an Easy API instance on the port you choose.
Authenticate WhatsApp: scan the QR code it prints with the phone, or use link-code login.
Open http://localhost:8080/api-docs/ to see the live session's interactive API docs, with generated Swagger and Postman files.

paths.name: Easy API
paths.for: Get a WhatsApp-backed HTTP API running in minutes
paths.what: One CLI command runs the runtime and an HTTP API with interactive docs and generated Swagger and Postman schemas.

paths.name: SocketClient
paths.for: Build a bot or worker without owning the browser runtime
paths.what: Your Node.js app connects to a running Easy API instance as a remote consumer. Commands go over HTTP RPC; runtime events arrive as Server-Sent Events.

paths.name: Embedded runtime
paths.for: Own the runtime inside your own Node.js app
paths.what: createClient gives your app control of browser selection, lifecycle and runtime behaviour.

paths.name: MCP server
paths.for: Let an AI agent use WhatsApp
paths.what: The built-in Model Context Protocol server exposes each Easy API method as a tool that agents such as Claude, Cursor and Windsurf can call.

useCases: Customer support inboxes that sync WhatsApp into your own tools
Order, booking and delivery notifications from internal systems
Bots that react to messages, group activity and runtime events
Webhook bridges for CRMs, helpdesks, automations and low-code tools
Multi-session automations with named accounts and isolated consumers
AI-agent workflows through the built-in Model Context Protocol server

capabilities.messages: Send and receive text, replies, forwards, reactions and edits; delete messages; pin and unpin.
capabilities.media: Images, video, documents, voice notes, view-once attachments, circular video notes and looping videos, with captions and quoted replies in typed options.
capabilities.groups: Read group activity and participant changes; create and join groups (Restricted licence).
capabilities.polls: Poll voting, synced results and vote listeners.
capabilities.events: Create, edit and cancel native WhatsApp event cards and handle RSVPs (going, not going, maybe). New in 5.5.
capabilities.stickers: Render WebP stickers locally with @open-wa/stickers (62 recipes in the first release, lazily loaded resources).
capabilities.multiSession: Run several named sessions (sessionId) side by side with isolated consumers.
capabilities.sessions: Compact encrypted session files you can move between containers with your own encryption key (5.4).
capabilities.refresh: Refresh a running session or apply a licence from the dashboard or with client.refresh() without restarting the Node process (5.5).
capabilities.drivers: Puppeteer, Playwright and an experimental Lightpanda driver.
capabilities.docs: Every running instance serves interactive API docs plus Swagger and Postman files.

licences.summary: The library is free to use. Some methods are marked as needing a licence key: method metadata marks each method none, insiders or restricted. A key is bought per WhatsApp number and passed at launch with --license-key or licenseKey.

free.name: No key
free.covers: Every method marked none, including reading chats, sending to existing contacts, media, polls, events, webhooks and MCP for those methods.

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.unlocks: Number profile and status checks (getNumberProfile, checkNumberStatus), orders, posting and reading status/stories, buttons, lists and other interactive messages (sendInteractive, sendButtons, sendListMessage), raw message payloads, starred messages, setting the profile picture.

tiers.name: Restricted
tiers.unlocks: Everything in Insiders, plus starting conversations with numbers that are not already contacts, creating groups and joining groups by invite link (createGroup, joinGroupViaLink, joinGroup).

legal.affiliation: This code is in no way affiliated with, authorised, maintained, sponsored or endorsed by WhatsApp or any of its affiliates or subsidiaries. This is independent and unofficial software.
legal.crypto: This distribution includes cryptographic software. Your country may restrict the import, possession, use or re-export of encryption software. The U.S. BIS classifies it as ECCN 5D002.C.1, eligible for License Exception ENC Technology Software Unrestricted (TSU).

http.note: Every method the session exposes is an HTTP endpoint on the running Easy API, documented live at /api-docs/. Any language that can make an HTTP request can use it (curl, PHP, Python, Go, n8n's HTTP node, a PBX script).
http.sendTextCurl:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/messages/sendText \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secure-key" \
  -d '{"to":"447700900123@c.us","content":"Your table is booked for 8pm.","options":{}}'
http.sendTextRoute: POST /api/messages/sendText with JSON {to, content, options}; response {success: true, data}
http.chatId: A chat ID is the full international number with no plus sign, spaces or dashes, followed by @c.us (groups end in @g.us).

jobs.name: Salon and clinic bookings
jobs.who: A developer building bookings for a salon, barber, clinic or studio on the business's own number
jobs.flow: A customer messages 'can I book a cut on Friday?'. The bot sends a poll of free times, books the one they tap, sends a WhatsApp event card for the appointment they can RSVP to, and reminds them the day before. Replies like 'running late' reach the staff.
jobs.licence: None for these methods when the customer messaged first. Starting a chat with a new number needs Restricted.

jobs.name: Hotel and appointment notifications
jobs.who: A developer sending booking confirmations, check-in details and reminders for a hotel, guesthouse, garage or any appointment business
jobs.flow: When a booking is made, the guest gets a confirmation, the address as a map pin and the booking PDF; the day before, a check-in reminder; replies go to the front desk.
jobs.licence: Guests who haven't messaged the hotel's number before are new numbers, so first messages to them need Restricted (£15 a month, checked 12 Oct 2026).

jobs.name: One-time codes (OTP)
jobs.who: A developer adding WhatsApp login or verification codes to an app
jobs.flow: Your app generates a code, sends it to the user's WhatsApp number from your own number, and the user types it back. Optionally check the number is on WhatsApp first.
jobs.licence: Codes go to numbers that haven't messaged you, so you need Restricted (£15 a month, checked 12 Oct 2026). checkNumberStatus needs Insiders, which Restricted includes.

jobs.name: WhatsApp calls and your PBX
jobs.who: A developer connecting a business's WhatsApp calls to a phone system, IVR or recorder
jobs.flow: Answer incoming WhatsApp calls with a greeting and record the caller, start calls, or stream call audio to and from your own system. Call state events tell you when a call rings, connects and ends.
jobs.licence: Calling is a licensed preview: it needs a calling-enabled licence key. Audio only; camera calls are in development.
jobs.audio: Streams are 16-bit little-endian PCM, 16 kHz, mono. A wss:// endpoint that speaks the OpenWA audio protocol can be a source or sink; most PBXs need a small adapter for their own socket format.

jobs.name: Stickers
jobs.who: Anyone whose bot or app should send stickers, for example turning a customer's photo into a sticker
jobs.flow: Give sendSticker a photo or video; open-wa renders it locally into a WebP sticker with the effects you list (62 recipes in this release, for example comic and sparkle) and sends it. The same renderer is a CLI for making sticker files.
jobs.licence: Not marked as licensed in the method list. Sending relies on the current sticker patch from the patch service.

jobs.name: Photos, voice notes, video and documents
jobs.who: Any bot or app that sends more than text
jobs.flow: Send images with captions, documents such as invoices and menus, voice notes, circular video notes, looping videos and view-once media; receive and decrypt media customers send.

jobs.name: Order and delivery updates
jobs.who: A developer connecting a shop or delivery system to WhatsApp
jobs.flow: Your shop's webhook calls the API when an order ships; the customer gets the update on WhatsApp and can reply with questions.
jobs.licence: None when the customer has messaged you before; Restricted to start new chats.

jobs.name: Support inbox
jobs.who: A team answering customers on WhatsApp from Chatwoot or their own helpdesk
jobs.flow: Messages to the business number appear as Chatwoot conversations and agents reply from Chatwoot, through @open-wa/integration-chatwoot.
jobs.licence: Follows the methods used; plain chat needs none.

jobs.name: An AI agent on WhatsApp
jobs.who: A developer letting Claude, Cursor or their own agent read and send WhatsApp messages
jobs.flow: Turn on the built-in MCP server; each Easy API method becomes a tool the agent can call.
jobs.licence: Follows the method each tool calls.
